cases.question: Which team should own this incident investigation now?

evidence.text: Billing endpoints timed out. The investigation established exhausted connections in the pool manager as the cause; the billing service only exposed the symptom.
The pool manager is owned by team oriole.
The billing service is owned by team sable.

cases.question: Which team should own this incident investigation now?

evidence.text: The message broker was initially suspected. A replay ruled that hypothesis out. The cause of the stalled deliveries remains undetermined.
The message broker belongs to team quartz.

cases.question: Which team should own this incident investigation now?

evidence.text: Initial diagnosis: a corrupted cache caused the search failures.
Correction to the initial diagnosis: the cache is healthy. We retract that finding; the confirmed fault is in the schema adapter.
The cache is maintained by team river.
The schema adapter belongs to team cedar.

cases.question: Which team should own this incident investigation now?

evidence.text: Investigation A concludes that the routing table corruption caused this incident and that the storage index was healthy.
Investigation B concludes that the storage index corruption caused this same incident and that the routing table was healthy. Neither investigation retracts its conclusion.
Team maple owns the routing table.
Team sable owns the storage index.

cases.question: Which team should own this incident investigation now?

evidence.text: This was not a resolver fault. DNS responses were correct throughout. The diagnosed cause was a certificate loader that discarded the new trust bundle.
Team quartz owns the resolver.
The certificate loader is assigned to team river.

cases.question: Which team should own this incident investigation now?

evidence.text: Checkout appeared broken because invoice workers rejected their generated mappings. The defect was isolated to the mapping compiler; the workers and checkout handlers behaved as specified.
Checkout handlers belong to team cedar.
Invoice workers belong to team oriole.
The mapping compiler is owned by team maple.

cases.question: Which team should own this incident investigation now?

evidence.text: A queue scheduler defect is one possibility, but the team has not reproduced it or selected it over the other hypotheses. No causal component has been established.
The queue scheduler belongs to team sable.

cases.question: Which team should own this incident investigation now?

evidence.text: The failing replay established the payload normalizer as the incident cause.
The payload normalizer is owned by team river. This is a current ownership record.
The payload normalizer is owned by team cedar. This is also a current ownership record; no precedence rule or replacement is recorded.

cases.question: Which team should own this incident investigation now?

evidence.text: The final investigation identifies the archive hydrator as the source of the outage.
The complete current directory lists the archive hydrator as unassigned; no team owns it.

cases.question: Which team should own this incident investigation now?

evidence.text: The preliminary report attributed the rejected uploads to the object gateway.
Replace the preliminary finding: the object gateway was not at fault. The final replay conclusively identified the checksum translator as the causal component.
Team oriole owns the object gateway.
Team quartz owns the checksum translator.

cases.question: Which team should own this incident investigation now?

evidence.text: Latency returned to normal after the rollout was paused, but the investigation did not isolate a trigger or establish which component caused the incident.
Team maple owns the deployment coordinator; team sable owns the latency collector.

cases.question: Which team should own this incident investigation now?

evidence.text: The first signed review attributes this outage solely to the lease allocator and explicitly excludes the shard monitor.
A second signed review attributes the same outage solely to the shard monitor and explicitly excludes the lease allocator. Both conclusions remain in force pending reconciliation.
Team cedar owns the lease allocator.
Team river owns the shard monitor.
